original_test_intent: Visually verify the exact BMC RJ45 indicator for active link, traffic activity and a lower-speed condition, while preserving undefined Amber Blink behavior.
original_method: An on-site operator identifies the management RJ45 and its link/activity indicators, stages approved normal-link, bounded management I/O and negotiated lower-speed conditions, records visible behavior, then restores and verifies management access.
manual_activity: A qualified operator labels the exact BMC management port, records its link/activity LEDs under approved link, traffic and lower-speed stages, and restores normal negotiation while another path monitors BMC availability.
required_inputs: BMC RJ45 physical port and separate link/activity LED mapping
Normal supported speed/duplex and exact link partner identity/configuration
Meaning of 'Down network speed': lower negotiated rate versus link down
Safe method to stage the lower rate without stranding management
Bounded management I/O flow, direction, duration and blink cadence
Amber Solid color mapping and assertion/clear timing
Amber Blink definition or revision-scoped N/A disposition
Independent console/OOB recovery and normal-link restoration
safety_requirements: Do not change the only management link without an independent recovery channel
Do not force speed/duplex using undocumented BMC commands or mismatched partner settings
Keep generated traffic bounded and management-safe
Verify the physical target; neighboring host NIC LEDs are not evidence
Do not claim color/cadence from software link counters
Stop on loss of reachability, negotiation loop, packet loss beyond limit, BMC fault, power or thermal anomaly; no automatic retry
agent_execution_scope: Verify source, port/LED mapping, topology and approved stimulus
Collect read-only link partner, negotiated speed/duplex, counters and BMC reachability
Prepare synchronized traffic/speed/visual timeline and package operator evidence
Confirm restored normal link through passive checks
Perform no speed force, cable action, BMC reset, traffic start, visual judgment, retry or verdict
engineer_actions: Define port LED legend, normal and lower-speed state matrix
Approve bounded I/O and safe speed staging with recovery
Resolve Amber Blink and timing criteria
Review visual plus link evidence and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Correctly states software cannot observe color/blink; it does not define or safely stage the source's I/O and down-speed conditions.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use operator-controlled visual acceptance with passive link/counter evidence; any traffic or negotiation change remains separately approved and bounded.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Green active/blink, Amber lower-speed, undefined Amber Blink and 15/5-minute estimates remain.

modernized_recommendation.status: MANUAL MANAGEMENT-PORT LED REVIEW WITH INDEPENDENT RECOVERY
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Capture contextual and close video synchronized to link negotiation and bounded traffic counters, stage a project-approved lower-rate partner profile, and verify normal-speed restoration through a separate recovery path.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact port/LED identity, measurable speed and traffic, cadence/timing, reachability monitoring and restoration without changing Master Criteria.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Software confirms link and traffic but not emitted LED color; Amber Blink remains unresolved and host-NIC LEDs are excluded.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: RJ45 jacks commonly contain separate link and activity LEDs whose color meanings vary with PHY and board wiring. A speed downgrade can also drop the only BMC session, so the same connection cannot be relied upon as both stimulus and recovery.

project_override_considerations: If auto-negotiation cannot safely produce the specified lower rate or amber is not supported on this board revision, engineering must define a revision-scoped alternative or N/A without substituting host NIC behavior.
expected_evidence: Approved port/LED/link-partner map and state matrix
Contextual and close video for active, bounded-I/O, lower-speed and restored stages
Negotiated speed/duplex, link/activity counters, traffic parameters and reachability timeline
Independent recovery availability and normal-link restoration
Amber Blink disposition, no-unapproved-speed-change/no-auto-retry audit, hashes and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently assigns green to active/I/O and Amber Solid to a down-speed condition, while explicitly leaving Amber Blink undefined. 'Down network speed' is ambiguous project input but no competing value is stated.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The defined link/activity/lower-speed states are manually testable after topology and safe-stimulus approval. Undefined Amber Blink remains pending without preventing static review.

review_improvement: Adds management-port identity, measurable negotiation/traffic, direct recovery protection and synchronized link evidence while retaining the undefined state.
independent_technical_reasoning: A BMC RJ45 may use one LED for link/activity and another for negotiated speed, with colors determined by PHY straps rather than software. The evidence must identify which emitter is observed and record the partner's negotiated rate. Generating I/O through the same management session can also alter or terminate observation, so independent reachability monitoring is needed to distinguish LED behavior from loss of the control path.
